channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes Seahawks TE AJ Barner “will likely see an uptick in production, as should backup TE Elijah Arroyo” this year.
item.description:
AJ Barner SEA Tight End

Destin notes that new Seahawks OC Brian Fleury served as the 49ers’ TE coach for four seasons “and is expected to feature the position prominently.” Aside from that, and an increase in shifts and motion, he thinks the offense is “going to look very similar” to last year. Barner underwent two offseason surgeries, one of which was to address a nagging ankle injury that Barner said he initially suffered during the 2024 Senior Bowl before the Seahawks drafted him. After turning in the PPR TE14 performance last season, Barner might have a shot to crack the position’s top 12.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes the Seahawks will feature RB Jadarian Price on early downs while RB George Holani plays the third-down, short-yardage and goal-line roles.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Destin reasonably wonders, “how much can Seattle feature Price as a pass catcher if he’s not trusted to block on third down?” He also thinks RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) will replace Holani whenever Charbonnet returns. Destin adds that “Price was not drafted as a direct replacement for Walker,” though he expects Price to handle a similar role. Losing high-value touches to Holani and Charbonnet could keep Price stuck in the RB3/FLEX tier, though, in a sense, he controls his own destiny and could force the coaching staff to increase his red zone usage with high-quality play.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Giants signed EDGE Malik Harrison, formerly of the Steelers, to the practice squad.
item.description:
Malik Harrison NYG Outside Linebacker

According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Harrison agreed to the deal “with the goal to contribute early.” The pass rusher totaled 28 tackles and seven quarterback pressures last year with the Steelers.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) “is not present for the media-access portion of practice.”
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Reiss also notes that the Patriots have three pre-Week 1 practices remaining, and Henderson has not practiced since August 24th, when he sustained the injury. One week ago, a Boston Globe report indicated Henderson should be “good to go” for Week 1 against the Seahawks. He still has time to get right, but veteran RB Rhamondre Stevenson can be treated as the team’s clear-cut lead back for the time being.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows said he is “sure” 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) “won’t be on the field for his usual 95 percent of the offensive snaps” in Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

While Barrows’ statement is agreeable, it leaves a lot of room for interpretation. The 32-year-old tight end is returning from an Achilles tendon rupture and was a close call to even make the trip to Australia, so a snap count of sorts makes sense. For fantasy managers who can afford to take a wait-and-see approach, it might be worthwhile. He has reportedly had a great recovery and his resumé is as good as it gets at the tight end position. He will likely be ranked as a low-end TE1 by default in Week 1 against the Rams.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows believes “the plan” is for WR De’Zhaun Stribling to be the primary slot receiver and WR Mike Evans’ “understudy” at X-receiver.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

In his projected depth chart, Barrows lists Stribling as both the starting slot receiver and the No. 2 X-receiver. He does not place Stribling on the Z-receiver depth chart, which could mean the rookie wide receiver has not yet earned a role in two-wide receiver sets. Veteran WR Deebo Samuel is the starting Z-receiver, though Barrows already reported that Samuel will take only “a portion” of the overall Z-receiver snaps. It would be surprising to see Nos. 2-3 Z-receivers, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing, play ahead of Stribling when Samuel needs a breather, but the season is long and Stribling can always change Barrows’ mind. Early in the year, Stribling is likely best treated as a WR4/FLEX candidate. Were Evans to miss time, Stribling would seemingly slide into a full-time starting role.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) resumed participating in team drills on Thursday.
item.description:
Nnamdi Madubuike BAL Defensive Lineman

Ravens coach Jesse Minter labeled Madubuike as “day-to-day” heading into Week 1. This does not necessarily mean Madubuike will take the field against the Colts next week, but it is a step in the right direction. Madubuike racked up 10 quarterback pressures, two sacks and three tackles in just two games played last year. Getting him back, even in a limited capacity, is a big deal.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said there is “nothing new to report” regarding CB Christian Gonzalez’s contract negotiations.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Vrabel’s comments concisely sum things up. Gonzalez, 24, is eligible for a contract extension but remains under contract through 2027 via his fifth-year option. The Patriots’ head coach notes that Gonzalez continues to grow as a player and remains competitive in practice.

Source: Chad Graff

item.title: Cardinals signed Michael Wilson to a three-year, $75 million extension through 2029.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal includes $47 million in guarantees, with a max value of $78 million. Wilson was set to enter a contract season in a week. Instead, he’ll be under contract with Arizona through the 2029 season. He broke out in the second half of the 2025 season and finished the year with his first 1,000-yard campaign. He compiled 775 of those yards in the final eight games of the year. Even if he can’t replicate those numbers over 17 weeks, Wilson took a massive step forward, and receivers aren’t cheap on the open market. It makes sense for Arizona to lock him up long-term instead of letting him test the waters of free agency next offseason.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Zay Flowers returned to practice Thursday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers suffered a quad bruise early in training camp but eventually returned to practice. He has been out of practice more recently with an undisclosed lower-body issue. His injuries have seemed relatively minor, and an appearance at practice today all but confirms that. Barring a setback, Flowers should be good to go as a high-end WR2 for Baltimore’s Week 1 opener versus the Colts.

Source: Sam Cohn

item.title: Cam Skattebo said he considered retiring after suffering his season-ending ankle injury.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Speaking on Up and Adams, Skattebo said he told himself in college that he would retire if he suffered a major injury. It’s a surprising comment on its face, but football fans shouldn’t be shocked that a young player questioned his choice of profession after suffering a gruesome ankle injury in his first season. Skattebo ultimately attacked rehab and returned faster than most people expected. He was a full-go early in the offseason and is now ready for Week 1.

Source: Up and Adams

item.title: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson will serve as the team’s backup quarterback.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Richardson spent training camp and the preseason battling it out with Riley Leonard for the backup gig. Given the arc of Richardson’s career, earning the backup gig is undoubtedly a win for the young passer. Richardson isn’t on the redraft fantasy radar, but dynasty managers can leave the light on for him.

Source: Stephen Holder

item.title: Chiefs restructured Trey Smith’s contract.
item.description:
Trey Smith KC Guard

Per Over the Cap’s Jason Fitzgerald, the move clears up $12.5 million in cap space. It also makes the Chiefs camp compliant ahead of the regular season, with some room to spare. Smith remains under contract through the 2028 season.

Source: Jason Fitzgerald

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes Mike Washington Jr. is “going to be a thing this year.”
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Rapoport reiterated the point, adding that Washington will be a weapon for the Raiders. The rookie running back was electric in the preseason, running for 168 yards on 23 attempts. Ashton Jeanty is expected to be ready for Week 1, but the team could use Washington to ease his workload early in the year. Washington may only be a FLEX play as long as Jeanty is healthy, but that’s still worth a flyer in fantasy drafts.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss reports “there’s been movement on Michael Wilson’s negotiations with the Cardinals.”
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Weinfuss adds that “something could come down in the next day or so.” Wilson has been in line for an extension this offseason and despite an effort, the Cardinals have yet to reach an agreement. It seems the sides are at least making progress, with Weinfuss hearing about “movement” in negotiations. Wilson was the team’s No. 1 wide receiver and downfield target for Jacoby Brissett after Kyler Murray went to the bench last season. An extension for the 26-year-old may be coming prior to Week 1.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports the Falcons plan for QB Michael Penix Jr. “to start eventually.”
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Wolfe added that head coach Kevin Stefanski does not want “an imaginary timeline” for Penix (knee) returning; the Falcons want to see him practice more and avoid rushing him back. The next week of practices will show if he is ready or if Tua Tagovailoa will be the “placeholder” for Week 1. Tagovailoa’s struggles seem to have made it a foregone conclusion that Penix will start when ready this season as the Falcons evaluate whether or not they will need to draft a quarterback in 2027.

Source: Cameron Wolfe

item.title: Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta said, “the fact that we didn’t put [DT Nnamdi Madubuike] on IR means that we would expect him to be able to contribute sooner than that.”
item.description:
Nnamdi Madubuike BAL Defensive Lineman

DeCosta added, “I’m probably more bullish on that right now than I even have been.” Madubuike’s 2025 season was cut short due to a neck injury and the 28-year-old has been working his way back since. He has been participating in individual drills but was not seen participating in team drills by the media in training camp. The Ravens chose to keep Madubuike off injured reserve, indicating they expect him to return less than four games into the regular season. The former third-round pick is a two-time Pro-Bowler and a key piece of the Ravens’ defensive line when healthy.

Source: Giana Han

item.title: Cowboys signed QB Joe Milton to their practice squad.
item.description:
Joe Milton DAL Quarterback

Milton initially made the 53-man roster but was let go after the initial wave of waiver claims. He went unclaimed when waivers ran Tuesday and now returns to the Cowboys on the practice squad. With Sam Howell winning the QB2 job, Milton will be QB3 heading into the season.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Ravens GM Eric DeCosta said he is “optimistic” about reaching a contract extension with Lamar Jackson.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

DeCosta also said he wants to get a deal done as soon as possible. Jackson currently has two seasons left on his five-year, $260 million contract. His cap hit for the 2026 season is a comfortable $34.4 million. That number balloons to $84.3 million next year. A new deal would help the Ravens spread Jackson’s cap hit over multiple seasons. Jackson is no longer one of the 10 highest-paid quarterbacks by average annual value, so he should also want to get a new deal on the books. It makes sense for both sides to come to an agreement sooner rather than later, ideally before the start of the season.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Nick Bosa (knee) said he is confident he will play in Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

Bosa suffered a torn ACL in Week 3 last year and is still working his way back. He was back on the practice field today and is on track to play in Australia versus the Rams next week. Bosa got off to a hot start last year, logging a sack in each of his first two games before exiting Week 3 a few snaps in. If he can return to form quickly, the 49ers defense should take a step forward this year.

Source: Josh Dubow

item.title: Ravens signed Chuma Edoga, formerly of the Jaguars.
item.description:
Chuma Edoga BAL Guard

Edoga appeared in 14 games for the Jags last year and made two starts. He has 25 career starts across both tackle spots and left guard. Edoga will be a versatile depth option for the Ravens.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports “there’s currently optimism” from the Bills that Khalil Shakir will play in Week 1 against the Texans.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

Shakir has been held out of practice for multiple weeks with an undisclosed injury. He has gotten some work off to the side, though it’s becoming more concerning with each day he fails to work in with the team. According to Zenitz, the team is simply being cautious with Shakir. We’ll learn more about his ailment when the first official injury report comes out next week. Like the Bills, fantasy managers should take a cautious approach with Shakir in the final week of drafts.

Source: Matt Zenitz

item.title: Jets hosted Justin Tucker for a workout.
item.description:
Justin Tucker

The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero notes that the Jets hosted a group workout and are exploring all options at kicker. They already claimed Blake Grupe and re-signed Jason Sanders to their practice squad this week. Tucker worked out for multiple teams last year after serving a 10-game suspension for violating the team’s personal conduct policy. He was never signed and hasn’t kicked in a game since the 2024 season, which was the worst of his career by far. Tucker made just 73.3 percent of his field goal tries.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Mike Evans (abductor) returned to practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans missed the bulk of training camp with quad, groin, and abductor injuries. The team took a cautious approach to his practice regimen during the offseason, and it seems to have paid off with him back on the field today. Evans’ status on the 49ers’ practice report next week will be one of the bigger storylines for the 49ers, but all signs point to him being healthy for Week 1. Fantasy managers can keep drafting him as a low-end WR2 for the final week of the summer.

Source: David Lombardi

item.title: Isaiah Bond (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Isaiah Bond CLE Wide Receiver

Browns head coach Todd Monken told reporters earlier in the week that Bond had cleared the league’s concussion protocol. It’s possible additional symptoms cropped up after he was cleared. With his return to play not going as expected, Bond could miss Cleveland’s opener versus the Jags. Fantasy managers can safely assume Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion, and Denzel Boston will be the team’s starting receiver trio in Week 1.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Panthers coach Dave Canales said he is “very optimistic” Jonathon Brooks will play in Week 1 against the Bears.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks is dealing with some soreness that the team hasn’t elaborated on any further. It’s likely maintenance for a player who has barely played any football over the past two seasons, but this is still a situation for fantasy managers to monitor. With Chuba Hubbard back at practice after missing time with a hamstring issue, we’re likely looking at a backfield by committee in Week 1. Both backs will be stuck in the RB3 ranks versus Chicago.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley said he expects J.J. McCarthy to be on the Week 1 roster.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

Teasley did not say whether McCarthy will be the backup or third-string quarterback. McCarthy is practicing in full after missing time with an ankle injury late in camp. His spotty play during training camp and the preseason, plus the missed time due to injury, all but guarantee Carson Wentz will be the team’s backup to open the year. As the QB3, McCarthy will likely be a healthy scratch, only able to enter the game if both quarterbacks ahead of him go down with injuries. The fact that he is expected to be on the Week 1 roster only means Teasley was unable to find someone willing to trade even a late-round pick for McCarthy.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Raiders named Kirk Cousins as the team’s Week 1 starter.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

With input from Tom Brady, head coach Klint Kubiak will put the 38-year-old Cousins under center for the season opener against the Dolphins. Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, will serve as Cousins’ backup. How long this arrangement will last is anyone’s guess. A good start to the regular season could delay Mendoza’s first NFL start for a couple months but he’s almost certain to take over as the Vegas starter at some point in 2026. Mendoza should be stashed in most superflex formats and Cousins profiles as a decent QB2 in such formats for Week 1.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s optimistic Ashton Jeanty (ankle) will play Week 1 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Kubiak smiled and said “yes” when asked if he thinks Jeanty will suit up for the season opener against Miami. Jeanty has been absent from practice since suffering an ankle sprain a week and a half ago, and the Raiders have danced around offering firm updates about Jeanty’s progress. If Jeanty doesn’t practice in full by next week he should be considered a real game-time call for Kubiak and the Raiders. Mike Washington, meanwhile, should be stashed in all fantasy leagues in case Jeanty is sidelined for a game or two.

Source: Levi Edwards

item.title: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s talking with Tom Brady “multiple times per week” about the team’s starting quarterback situation.
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

An NFL head coach consulting with an NFL announcer on who his team should start under center is a brave new world for the league. It looks like the Raiders are set on Kirk Cousins to start Week 1 against the Dolphins after Fernando Mendoza’s spotty preseason play and struggles in training camp. Look for Cousins to target his short-area pass catchers relentlessly, like he did last year in Atlanta. It won’t be long before Mendoza gets a shot at starting duties. He should be rostered in most superflex leagues.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (soreness) worked to the side of practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks has now worked to the side in two straight practices and Panthers coaches are being cagy about his ailment. It’s not a great develop less than two weeks ahead of Carolina’s season opener. Chub Hubbard, meanwhile, is back at practice after being sidelined with a hamstring injury for a couple weeks. Brooks’ practice status will be very much worth monitoring in the coming days. He appears to be nothing more than a touchdown-dependent flex for right now.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Cardinals have “attempted” to sign Michael Wilson to a contract extension.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson emerged as the team’s clear No. 1 receiver in 2025 once Kyler Murray was benched in favor of Jacoby Brissett, who has the arm strength to get the ball downfield to Wilson. Wilson was 18th among all wideouts in receiving yards and tenth in air yards last year. Fowler said “the likeliest path for Wilson is to enter Week 1 on the final year of his rookie deal. Perhaps the team finds a way to get a deal done, but sources indicate he’s likely to be a key free agent.” Wilson, 26, could make Alec Pierce money in 2027 if the Cardinals don’t re-sign him in the coming months.

Source: ESPN.com

item.title: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Jeanty’s status for Week 1 against the Dolphins remains very much in the air more than a week after he sustained a possible high ankle sprain in practice. If he’s still not practicing by the end of the week, he might be on the wrong side of questionable for the season opener. Mike Washington, who has drawn rave reviews from Raiders coaches, would be in line for a starter’s workload if Jeanty is sidelined.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Texans are “prepared to put CJ Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club.”
item.description:
C.J. Stroud HOU Quarterback

Houston GM Nick Caserio recently said the team would not negotiate a new deal with Stroud once the regular season begins, putting a hard and fast deadline on Stroud’s ability to secure a longer-term contract with the team that drafted him. His immense and nationally-televised struggles down the stretch last season — including his playoff meltdown against the Patriots — could factor into the team’s decision to go all in on him as a long-term franchise quarterback. Fowler said Stroud “can let an exploding quarterback market do the work for him if he waits an additional six to eight months” and explore free agency in 2027. Stroud over the past three seasons ranks 22nd out of 40 qualifying QBs in adjusted EPA per drop back, alongside Bo Nix and Trevor Lawrence. He ranks 24th in drop back success rate, just behind Mac Jones.

Source: ESPN.com

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (toe) worked to the side of practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka has been held out with a lingering toe issue ahead of Week 1. That he’s working to the side today is probably a positive development for the second-year wideout, though we would like to see him practice in full by the end of this week or the start of next week. After a hot start to the 2025 season, Egbuka was almost unusable for fantasy purposes over the season’s final couple months. He’ll look to bounce back in 2026 with a disgruntled Baker Mayfield at full health.

item.title: Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham said the team is evaluating “all” of its quarterback options ahead of Week 1.
item.description:
Jack Strand ATL Quarterback

It appears to be careful language in describing how the team is approaching its iffy QB situation ahead of the season opener against the Steelers. Rookie QB Jack Strand, who played well in his preseason appearances, had taken some first-team reps over the past month with Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa struggling with injuries and plagued by poor play. It’s unclear whether Penix will be 100 percent ready for the season opener, while Tagovailoa has been shockingly bad in training camp and during the preseason. Strand is a decent bench stash in deeper superflex formats for now.

Source: D. Orlando Ledbetter

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he would be “pleasantly surprised” if LeQuint Allen Jr. (soft tissue) played in Week 1 against the Browns.
item.description:
LeQuint Allen

Coen talked up Ameer Abdullah as a potential replacement for Allen’s duties in pass protection. He also singled out Chris Rodriguez’s abilities in pass pro. Pass protection duties aren’t a direct source of fantasy value, but it usually means that player will be on the field for the two-minute drill, which can generate plenty of receptions for running backs. Bhayshul Tuten not getting those reps would be a notable ding to his fantasy outlook. Allen himself isn’t on the fantasy radar, healthy or not.

Source: Michael DiRocco

item.title: Lions GM Brad Holmes said he hopes Isiah Pacheco (back, IR) returns this season.
item.description:
Isiah Pacheco DET Running Back

Holmes didn’t offer a timetable for Pacheco’s return. The former Chief injured his knee early in camp and then suffered a back injury, which ultimately landed him on injured reserve. He will miss at least the first four games of the season while on IR, though it sounds like a Week 5 return isn’t in the cards. For now, Jacob Saylors will serve as Jahmyr Gibbs’ backup. He shouldn’t see much work as long as Gibbs is healthy, but dynasty managers may want to give him a look on the waiver wire.

Source: Eric Woodyard

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was a “full go” in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

BTJ suffered a shoulder injury late in camp and has dealt with shoulder issues in the past, so this latest scare was a definite concern for fantasy managers and Jags fans alike. The good news is that he’s practicing in full over a week before the first game of the season. After a summer of hype for Parker Washington, Thomas Jr. is likely second in the pecking order for targets. Barring a setback with the shoulder injury, he should project for WR3 numbers in Jacksonville’s opener versus the Browns.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Chuba Hubbard will lead the Panthers backfield in 2026.
item.description:
Chuba Hubbard CAR Running Back

The team’s plan, per Graziano, is for Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks to split carries this season. That comes as little surprise. “If Hubbard stays healthy, he’s the one in whom they’ve built up more trust, so I’d expect him to be the one the Panthers lean on to try to grind out games when they have the lead,” Graziano said. “The split should be pretty close, but it would not be a surprise at all to get to the end of the season and see that Hubbard got the majority of the work.” Brooks on Tuesday practiced to the side while Hubbard (hamstring) practiced in full. It’s a concerning situation for those who have gone in on Brooks as Carolina’s lead back.

Source: ESPN.com

item.title: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Jameson Williams could lead the Lions in receiving this season.
item.description:
Jameson Williams DET Wide Receiver

Graziano said the “Lions offense is going to hum this season, and Williams is the player poised to take the biggest leap.” That leap, he said, could come as Detroit coaches push Jamo “to expand his route repertoire and contribute as more than just a deep threat.” That in turn could create more short-area and intermediate opportunities and make Williams something more than a boom-bust WR3 play. Williams’ splits with and without Sam LaPorta are concerning, but he should be a high-upside swing in fantasy drafts, especially for those who fade receivers in the first couple rounds.

Source: ESPN.com

item.title: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Isaiah Likely could be a “breakout star” in the Giants offense this season.
item.description:
Isaiah Likely NYG Tight End

Graziano affirmed what every fantasy manager believes: Likely will probably be the team’s WR2 behind Malik Nabers this season. New York coaches, according to Graziano, “love the way he has embraced and evolved his relationship with Jaxson Dart since he has been in New York. Likely is a regular visitor to the quarterback room, and the connection he has formed with Dart on and off the field could pay major dividends.” Graziano said Likely could be Dart’s top option if Nabers needs time to get back to full speed as he recovers from his 2025 ACL injury. Likely profiles as an easy click for fantasy drafters who forgo the game’s elite tight ends.

Source: ESPN.com

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports George Kittle (Achilles) traveled with the 49ers to Australia.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

This, according to Rapoport, comes after “two positive days” of practice for the veteran tight end, coming off a late-season Achilles injury. Kittle is “trending in the right direction” to play against the Rams in the first game of the NFL season, and the first-ever game in Australia. It’s possible the 49ers will have a pitch count for Kittle coming into the season. If he suits up against the Rams, Kittle will be a risky low-end TE1 option in 12-team leagues. He had nine catches for 84 yards and a touchdown in his only game against LA in 2025.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Vikings signed LB Kyle Van Noy, formerly of the Ravens, to their practice squad.
item.description:
Kyle Van Noy MIN Outside Linebacker

Van Noy spent time with Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores in both Miami and New England, making this a reunion for the two. The 35-year-old linebacker spent the past three seasons with the Ravens, tallying 12.5 sacks during a 2024 Pro Bowl campaign. The Vikings will start Van Noy out on the practice squad, but fans shouldn’t be surprised to see him in the middle of the Minnesota defense later this season.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: NOF Network’s Nick Underhill reports Saints RB Kendre Miller will be “fine” after he left practice early Tuesday with a “minor issue.”
item.description:
Kendre Miller NO Running Back

Miller left practice early under his own power Tuesday, an all-too-familiar picture for the oft-injured back coming off an ACL tear from last October. However, Underhill reports it is a minor issue for the 24-year-old. With Alvin Kamara (knee) missing time, Miller has seen a lot of preseason work. Miller, when healthy, can be the Saints’ RB2 and primary handcuff to Travis Etienne.

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: Ravens signed TE Nick Vannett to their practice squad.
item.description:
Nick Vannett BAL Tight End

Vannett, 33, is a journeyman veteran tight end best known for his blocking skills. Starting his career with the Seahawks, he has jumped around the league with the Steelers, Broncos, Saints, Giants, Chargers, Titans, Vikings, and Rams. He signed with the Seahawks in the offseason but was let go in final cuts. The Ravens add Vannett as blocking tight end depth on the practice squad.

Source: Jeff Zrebiec

item.title: Dolphins signed RB Jarquez Hunter to their practice squad.
item.description:
Jarquez Hunter MIA Running Back

Hunter was notably acquired for Tutu Atwell in the preseason but was released during final cuts. The Dolphins now bring him back as depth in the running back room. Also notably on the practice squad is former first-round defensive lineman Mazi Smith. The Dolphins rounded out the practice squad with RB Carlos Washington, WR Jalen Reagor, WR Will Sheppard, CB Ethan Bonner, DE Max Llewellyn, TE Tre Watson, OT Gottlieb Ayedze, DL Jordan Miller, EDGE Clelin Ferrell, EDGE Amari Gainer, EDGE Rodney McGraw, LB Liam Anderson, CB Jaylin Simpson, and S Major Burns.

item.title: Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht said WR Ted Hurst is “going to play a role” this season.
item.description:
Ted Hurst TB Wide Receiver

Licht said Hurst was initially slated for a learning role behind the deep Buccaneers wide receiver corps. However, he added that the rookie 22-year-old has “proven to us throughout camp, even OTAs, practice every day that he’s been very, very steady...it’s kind of evolved into okay, we can use him this year and he’s going to play a role.” Hurst has received generally positive reports out of training camp. With Emeka Egbuka and Jalen McMillan continuing to deal with injuries throughout preseason, Hurst has gotten more opportunities and proven to the front office he can be used as a rookie. When Egbuka, McMillan, and Chris Godwin are all healthy, Hurst will have a tough time putting up fantasy-relevant production. However, given various active injuries and the injury history of the Bucs’ wide receiver room, he is certainly worth a late-round pick for fantasy purposes.

Source: MicNuggets

item.title: Texans signed DE Chris Braswell, formerly of the Buccaneers, to their practice squad.
item.description:
Chris Braswell HOU Outside Linebacker

Braswell is a former 2024 second-round pick that could not get it going with the Bucs. He now joins a formidable defense on the Texans’ practice squad. Houston also adds WR Mitchell Tinsley; he is a former Bengals preseason standout who has a path to contributing for the Texans’ injured wide receiver group. Also signed to the Texans’ practice squad are RB Jawhar Jordan, RB Noah Whittington, WR Lewis Bond, WR Josh Kelly, WR Daniel Sobkowicz, TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden, OT James Neal III, C Ka’ena Decambra, DT Dominic Bailey, LB Jamal Hill, CB Bryce Hall, CB Alijah Huzzie, and S George Odum.

item.title: Cowboys signed OT Wanya Morris, formerly of the Falcons, to their practice squad.
item.description:
Wanya Morris DAL Offensive Lineman

Morris started several games for the Chiefs at left tackle over the past three seasons before the Falcons acquired him in the offseason. Atlanta chose to part ways and now the Cowboys add Morris as tackle depth heading into the season. Also signed to the Cowboys’ initial practice squad are RB Israel Abanikanda, WR Jordan Hudson, WR Anthony Smith, TE Michael Trigg, TE Mitchell Van Vooren, OT Marcellus Johnson, OL Nick Leverett, DT Tommy Dunn, DT Elijah Garcia, DT Adedayo Odeleye, LB Justin Barron, LB Isaiah Land, LB Curtis Robinson, CB Derion Kendrick, and CB Reddy Steward.

item.title: Raiders GM John Spytek said Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is in a “good spot” and said “I expect him to be back as quick he can, maybe quicker than some people would expect. When that is, we’ll see.”
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Well, yes, we will see. The Raiders haven’t really given much of an indication from the inside on when Jeanty will return, but he wasn’t placed on injured reserve on cutdown day (he can still be placed there before the start of Week 1) and so long as it the location of his ankle sprain remains low and not high, we’re generally optimistic that Jeanty can make it back in the first month of the season.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Chargers signed QB DJ Uiagalelei to their practice squad.
item.description:
DJ Uiagalelei LAC Quarterback

As it was last year, Uiagalelei remains in town after losing the backup gig to Trey Lance. Also signed to Los Angeles’ practice squad are: LB Lander Barton, LB Andre Carter, DL Jahmeer Carter, LB Junior Colson, RB Gregory Desrosiers, WR Gary Jennings, RB Amar Johnson, C Josh Kaltenberger, DB Nikko Reed, WR Devonte Ross, TE Evan Svoboda, LB Nadame Tucker, T Laekin Vakalahi, DB Isas Waxter, DL Terry Webb, OLB Caleb Murphy and CB Kaiir Elam.

item.title: Browns signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to their practice squad.
item.description:
Jaleel McLaughlin CLE Running Back

Outside of Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Raheim Sanders are also in front of McLaughlin. The 25-year-old back has landed in a nice enough spot though considering none of these backs outside of Judkins has proved all that much yet. Also joining the Browns practice squad are: CB Myles Bryant. DE Logan Fano. T KT Leveston. P Wes Pahl. CB D’Angelo Ross. DT Tyreak Sapp. DE Khordae Sydnor. S Zion Washington. LB Nathaniel Watson and WR Kole Wilson.

item.title: Bengals signed QB Josh Johnson to their practice squad.
item.description:
Josh Johnson CIN Quarterback

It really strains the limits of credulity to have a 40-year-old practice squad player, but here we are. johnson remains QB3 in Cincinnati after being released at last cuts. Also on Cincy’s practice squad are: RB Kentrel Bullock, QB Sean Clifford, DT Howard Cross, DE Isaiah Foskey, LB Joe Giles-Harris, LB Shaka Heyward, DB Bralyn Lux, RB Kendall Milton, WR Jordan Moore, WR Noah Thomas and DB Russ Yeast.

item.title: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Bijan Robinson fantasy managers “may not like how many goal-line carries [Brian Robinson] gets.”
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Thanks, we hate it. [Brian] Robinson has “shown a physical style in practice that cements his role as the new Tyler Allgeier” per Kendall. We don’t think one isolated report should dissuade anyone from picking Bijan Robinson 1.1 in drafts, but it has the potential to be a headache if it comes to pass. It must be said that only the Falcons could create a scenario where a Robinson scores and nobody knows whether to be upset or happy until we get a clarification on which one.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Free agent LB Kyle Van Noy visited with the Vikings on Tuesday.
item.description:
Kyle Van Noy

Van Noy played with Flores in Miami and New England, and the Vikings could use some more depth at edge rusher. It would be an unsurprising reunion.

item.title: Joe Milton was not claimed on waivers.
item.description:
Joe Milton

He’ll likely catch on with a practice squad in the next day or two, perhaps with the Cowboys again. Milton had initially made the 53-man roster in Dallas but lost his spot when they claimed Emari Demercado off waivers. The 26-year-old has an arm that was made to play quarterback and a decision-making process that was made to play quarterback in 1975.

Source: Nick Harris

item.title: Aaron Rodgers said Roman Wilson had a “fantastic camp.”
item.description:
Roman Wilson PIT Wide Receiver

It was a bit of a compliment sandwich, with Rodgers opening his comments by mentioning a route Wilson screwed up early in camp and again today. Rodgers did, however, say Wilson will have to play a big role for the team and that he has the utmost confidence in him. Rodgers is infamously punitive to his younger players, and the Steelers have second-round rookie Germie Bernard behind Wilson on the depth chart. Wilson is firmly ahead of Bernard for now, but one mistake during the regular season could flip the WR3 role in an instant.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Jakobi Meyers (thumb) returned to practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers missed some time late in training camp with a thumb issue that forced him to wear a brace on his right hand. Coen specifically said that Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was practicing in full and didn’t say the same of Meyers. It’s possible the team is working Meyers in more slowly as the season approaches. Still, even a limited practice more than a week ahead of Week 1 should put Meyers in line to play. Meyers will be in a supporting role behind Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr . this year. He will be a low-end FLEX play for the Jags’ opener versus Cleveland.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Saints claimed CB Decamerion Richardson off waivers from the Raiders.
item.description:
Decamerion Richardson NO Cornerback

Richardson, a 2024 fourth-round pick, started seven games in 2024 and has been a big part of Raiders special teams. He’ll try to hang on to a roster spot with the Saints.

item.title: Theo Johnson (shoulder) participated in practice Tuesday wearing a non-contact jersey.
item.description:
Theo Johnson NYG Tight End

John Harbaugh has said that Johnson “will be fine,” but we’re going to cover our bases on this one with the Giants keeping five tight ends. Johnson has a week and change to get healthy for Sunday Night Football in Week 1.

Source: Art Stapleton

item.title: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell reports the Chiefs view Kenneth Walker as a potential three-down back.
item.description:
Kenneth Walker KC Running Back

What is clear in the wake of the Chiefs waiving Emari Demercado is that they don’t really have another player that qualifies as a passing-down back besides Walker without squinting. The other backs they kept are Emmett Johnson, a Day 3 rookie, and Brashard Smith, a gadget player without enough size to really block. Perhaps the Chiefs will address this in street free agency ahead of the season, but as things stand, it certainly seems like Walker will be involved on all three downs.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Lions placed RB Isiah Pacheco (back) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Isiah Pacheco DET Running Back

It’s a familiar place for the 27-year-old running back. He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season. It sounds like former UFL star Jacob Saylors will enter Week 1 as the favorite for whatever portion of the carries Jahmyr Gibbs doesn’t take, not that it figures to be many.

item.title: Asked if he would play in Week 1 without a new contract, Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. said “I don’t know. I’ve got to talk to he guys upstairs (in the front office) and my agents about that one.”
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

We haven’t had much in the way of contract beefs this offseason, but Porter Jr. seems ready to make up for lost time here. The Steelers CB spent most of training camp on the active/PUP list with a “back injury.” It seems like there’s at least a real chance he skips out on Week 1 to prove a point if he isn’t paid.

Source: Mike DeFabo

item.title: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Broderick Jones will compete with Terence Steele for the starting right tackle job.
item.description:
Broderick Jones DAL OFFENSIVE TACKLE (SUB)

This is a bit surprising because the Cowboys had already had a competition for Tyler Guyton on the left side (that Guyton won), and it was assumed that Jones would come in and add to that competition. Not so fast. Steele just received a three-year contract this offseason and is on the books for a $15.2 million cap hit in 2027, so we’d be surprised if Jones won the job.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Cardinals placed TE Tip Reiman on the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
Tip Reiman ARI Tight End

He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season. Reiman went down with a gruesome leg injury in Week 5 against the Titans and was put in an air cast. Hunter Long, who the Cardinals acquired at last cuts, will likely fill in Reiman’s role early on this season.

item.title: Alvin Kamara (knee) is not practicing on Tuesday.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

This isn’t a surprise, as Kamara’s timeline to return per Adam Schefter as of August 19 was a month away. What was a minor surprise is that Kamara wasn’t placed on injured reserve before the start of the season. Perhaps there is still a chance he can go in Week 1, though we’d call him doubtful at this point based on the initial timeline.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Eagles placed TE Grant Calcaterra on injured reserve.
item.description:
Grant Calcaterra PHI Tight End

It’s unknown what injury he has at this time. Calcaterra will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. It doesn’t seem like Eagles fans are particularly upset about this. Assuming they don’t bring in Zach Ertz as a secondary tight end, Johnny Mundt and Eli Stowers figure to be the main players behind Dallas Goedert this year.

item.title: Raiders placed EDGE Keyron Crawford on season-ending injured reserve.
item.description:
Keyron Crawford LV Defensive End

The rookie third-round pick suffered a season-ending Achilles injury in his final preseason game. Crawford will likely pick things back up next year with a chance to make real noise for the Raiders — and perhaps without Maxx Crosby in front of him — assuming no setbacks.

item.title: Jaguars placed OL Patrick Mekari (back) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Patrick Mekari

Mekari, who underwent back surgery, will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. We’d bet on him missing more than four. Emmanuel Pregnon seems likely to start at left guard for the Jaguars as a rookie.

item.title: Saints signed WR Cedric Tillman to their practice squad.
item.description:
Cedric Tillman NO Wide Receiver

In theory Tillman could put pressure on the back of the Saints wideout corps. In actuality, if they really thought that, they probably would have signed him to the active roster. Still, with only four healthy wideouts on the roster, Tillman could be elevated early. Zamir White is the other big name on the Saints practice squad and is joined by TE Stone Smartt, DE Fadil Diggs, RB CJ Donaldson, DB TJ Hall Jr., T Alan Herron, T Easton Kilty, WR Jalen Moreno-Cropper, WR Trey Palmer, LB Jackson Sirmon, K Charlie Smyth, DL Jay’Viar Suggs and T Alex Wollschlaeger

item.title: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Carnell Tate is “working out some stiffness” and did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Carnell Tate TEN Wide Receiver

This is, to be a broken record, probably not much to be concerned about just yet. The 21-year-old Tate is in a weird spot as a clear high-volume target on a passing offense that has not looked good all preseason and probably should be eyed skeptically heading into 2026. Nevertheless, Tate has the goods to be a fantasy producer this year if the offense around him is good enough to let that happen.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

Neither did Ty Johnson (knee), with both players still having plenty of time to get back before next Sunday’s Week 1 game against the Texans. It’s hard to tell how seriously to take these because Joe Brady has been a brick wall on injury questions, but we’ll get a better indication next week when injury reports start to hit.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Bills placed Tyrell Shavers (knee) on the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
Tyrell Shavers BUF Wide Receiver

He’ll miss at least the first four weeks of the season after tearing his ACL in the playoffs. No surprise there. Shavers will likely be a late-season reinforcement, if that, in 2026 after coming on strong when the Bills needed receiving help last year.

item.title: Patriots placed EDGE Harold Landry on the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
Harold Landry NE Outside Linebacker

The 30-year-old edge will miss at least the first four games of the season. He barely practiced this offseason and never got off the active/PUP list. It remains to be seen if Landry will get healthy enough to play this season.

item.title: Jets claimed K Blake Grupe off waivers from the Colts.
item.description:
Blake Grupe NYJ Kicker

Jason Sanders, who had won the Jets kicker competition, is instead released to make way for Grupe. As we wrote about Sanders a few days ago: Winning the Jets kicker competition is not an endorsement that provides many fantasy points. Grupe will probably be stuck in the 20s in weekly ranks in most of the Jets games this year.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Steelers signed RB Lew Nichols to the practice squad.
item.description:
Lew Nichols PIT Running Back

The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes Nicholes is the player he’d promote to join the carries split if either Jaylen Warren or Rico Dowdle is injured. Perhaps that’s enough of an endorsement to get him on the deep dynasty radar. RB Travis Homer, DB Doneiko Slaughter, WR Brandon Smith, WR Max Hurleman, OL Doug Nester, OL Steven Jones, DL Esezi Otomewo, DL Kyler Baugh, DB Sebastian Castro, LB Jacoby Windmon, TE Lake McRee and DE Julius Welschof were also signed to the practice squad.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes Omar Cooper Jr.'s role “should grow over time.”
item.description:
Omar Cooper NYJ Wide Receiver

Cooper “started to show some signs of life by the end” of training camp. The first-rounder will split time with Isaiah Williams in the slot and also operate “as a gadget player.” Keep him out of lineups early, but he is still on the dynasty radar and should be monitored on the waiver wire in shallow leagues.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Ja’Marr Chase (knee) will be “limited this week” but that he “feels good about his progress.”
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

We’re not viewing this as a major cause for concern, the Bengals have no reason to rush Chase back on the field after he hyperextended his knee last week. If he’s still drawing limited tags on the official injury reports next week, then we can start Panic Mode. Taylor added that Higgins (head contusion) may also be limited this week. "(Tee) and Ja’Marr will be good at the end of the week,” said Taylor.

Source: Charlie Goldsmith

item.title: Raiders placed EDGE Keyron Crawford on season-ending injured reserve.
item.description:
Keyron Crawford LV Defensive End

The rookie third-round pick suffered a season-ending ankle injury in his final preseason game. Crawford will likely pick things back up next year with a chance to make real noise for the Raiders — and perhaps without Maxx Crosby in front of him — assuming no setbacks.

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Tank Dell (knee) is “close” but “not quite there.”
item.description:
Tank Dell HOU Wide Receiver

He was already placed on injured reserve, so he’ll miss the first four games of the season. Reading between the lines it sounds like Dell has a chance to miss more than just the first four games of the season. Kayshon Boutte and Dalton Schultz will battle for the role of lead secondary target behind Nico Collins while Dell is sidelined.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio said there were “productive talks” on a contract extension for QB C.J. Stroud and that if a deal isn’t done before the start of the season, they’ll pick it up next offseason.
item.description:
C.J. Stroud HOU Quarterback

There’s really no reason for Stroud to want to negotiate off last year’s end-of-season performance, so we’re not stunned that there’s been no extension. It does sound like the Texans are at least laying the groundwork for next offseason. The general NFL expectation has been that Stroud will go into the year without an extension. The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan Alexander reported that league sources believe the Texans and Stroud’s camp “are not far off on what they think Stroud’s contract terms should look like and how much he should be paid per year.”

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Keylan Rutledge would start at left guard.
item.description:
Keylan Rutledge HOU Guard

He called him “their best offensive lineman.” The big news here is that free-agent addition Wyatt Teller will start on the bench with Evan Brown starting at center. We’ll see if the Texans have finally hit on a formula that will help them run the ball, but it’s not great news for Teller that even the Texans don’t want to start him.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said WR Savion Williams (ankle/IR) has a high-ankle sprain.
item.description:
Savion Williams GB Wide Receiver

Williams was placed on IR at last cuts without an explanation of the injury, so here it is. Gutekunst said he thinks Williams will be ready when the four-week mandatory stay on IR is over.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said the team traded for Kyle McCord to be the team’s No. 2 quarterback, but that he expects recently-claimed Brady Cook to “make a push.”
item.description:
Kyle McCord MIA Quarterback

Riveting situation. The main fantasy takeaway here is probably something like “if Malik Willis gets hurt this year, all Dolphins pass-catchers will take major downgrades.”

Source: David Furones

item.title: Browns signed CB Noah Igbinoghene.
item.description:
Noah Igbinoghene CLE Defensive Back

Igbinoghene didn’t survive last cuts with the Commanders, but catches on as a depth add in Cleveland. The 2020 first-rounder is entering his age-27 season. The Browns waived Michael Coats Jr. in a corresponding move.

item.title: Texans signed TE Brevin Jordan.
item.description:
Brevin Jordan HOU Tight End

He was released at last cuts, but comes back as the Texans created extra roster space with a few injured reserve placements. DL Dominique Robinson also re-signed with the team.

Source: ProFootballTalk on NBCSports.com

item.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio said the team has placed RT Braden Smith (foot) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Braden Smith HOU Tackle

Smith and OL Sam Hagen (undisclosed) will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season. The 30-year-old Smith was a priority free agent target for the Texans. Trent Brown will likely draw the starting nod at right tackle.

Source: ProFootballTalk on NBCSports.com

item.title: Lions signed TE Tyler Conklin.
item.description:
Tyler Conklin DET Tight End

They released him on Sunday, but it was merely roster manipulation as vested veterans aren’t subject to waivers. The 31-year-old should play a role as one of Detroit’s lower-end tight ends behind Sam LaPorta.

Source: Matt Zenitz

item.title: Browns signed EDGE Sam Williams to a one-year contract.
item.description:
Sam Williams CLE Outside Linebacker

Williams was let go by the Cowboys at last cuts. He’ll become a part of a new-look EDGE room built around Jared Verse in Cleveland. Williams managed just one sack and six additional tackles for loss in 474 snaps with the Cowboys last year.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (toe) did not practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka was given a ringing “hopefully” response from Todd Bowles when asked if he’d play in Week 1. We’re not overly concerned just yet, but he’s going to need to practice at some point to play. Jalen McMillan (knee) also sat, though we’re not as concerned about him since he’s practiced on that knee injury.

Source: Jenna Laine

item.title: Colts GM Chris Ballard said Keenan Allen will play in Indianapolis’ Week 1 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Keenan Allen IND Wide Receiver

In other words, there will be no in-house punishment for Allen being arrested for DWI and DWI endangering a person on Sunday morning. It’s a hard-to-augur game, as we are not entirely sure if the Ravens defense is going to take a turn for the better and if Daniel Jones is NFL-healthy rather than training-camp-healthy, but Allen should have enough of a role to land in the WR4 ranks at the very least.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) returned to practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

He missed about a week with the ailment, and reporters discovered that the “lower body injury” was a groin injury. We wouldn’t be surprised if he were limited a bit over the next two weeks, but if he’s practicing he’s certainly likely to play in Week 1.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Jonathon Brooks worked to the side of practice on Tuesday.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

We’re not sure what Brooks is dealing with but his practice status will be something to monitor in the coming days. Chuba Hubbard, meanwhile, is practicing in full after missing weeks with a hamstring issue. Brooks headed into 2026 with a chance to be the Panthers’ lead back after fighting back through a series of catastrophic injuries. Carolina’s backfield could prove frustrating for fantasy purposes this season.

Source: Danielle Stein

item.title: Colts general manager Chris Ballard said he expects Anthony Richardson, Jr. to remain with the team in 2026.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

Richardson is listed alongside Riley Leonard as the team’s QB2 for now. Either Leonard or Richardson — who struggled in the preseason — will serve as Daniel Jones’ backup this season. One of the most inaccurate passers in modern NFL history, Richardson would be a massive downgrade for all Indy pass catchers if he finds his way under center in 2026.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: 49ers general manager John Lynch said he hopes Mike Evans (adductor) will practice next week.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans’ Week 1 status is starting to look iffy after missing most of the past few weeks with various injuries. Entering his age-33 season, Evans will need to log at least a couple practices next week if he’s going to suit up against the Rams in the season opener. Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans is “ahead of schedule doing good. But we know with Mike and where he is at in his career, we’ll definitely have to treat him differently.” An Evans absence would be a marked boost for De’Zhaun Stribling and perhaps Deebo Samuel. Evans will be a name to watch in the coming days.

Source: David Lombardi

item.title: Tyler Warren (groin) practiced Tuesday.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren is recovering from an apparently minor groin injury. By all accounts he should be a full go for Week 1. Warren last season was top three among tight ends in targets per route run and first-read target rate in the balanced Colts offense. He’ll offer a sturdy weekly floor and could lead the team in targets in 2026 if he stays healthy.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Alec Pierce (ankle) practiced Tuesday.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce missed most of training camp while recovering from offseason ankle surgery after signing a huge contract extension with the Colts. Pierce appears on track to suit up for Week 1. Whether Pierce is on some sort of pitch count remains to be seen. Pierce should eventually function as the team’s WR1, operating as more than a strictly downfield threat. He should be seen as a flex play for now.

Source: James Boyd

item.title: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) was not seen at practice Tuesday.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

Jeanty remains sidelined ahead of the Raiders’ Week 1 matchup against the Dolphins after sustaining a potentially high ankle sprain last week. Meanwhile, rookie RB Mike Washington “has changed the staff’s perspective of the running back room,” according to ESPN’s Ryan McFadden with some impressive play during training camp and in the preseason. Head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s “not making any promises on percentages of play time” for Washington or Jeanty ahead of the season opener. Jeanty could be a while before he’s ready to take on a true workhorse role in the Vegas backfield. Washington should be rostered in all fantasy formats for now.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Bucs general manager Jason Licht said there are no immediate plans to re-open contract talks with Baker Mayfield.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Licht during a Wednesday presser said the Bucs were “on to Cincinnati” with the regular season less than two weeks away. Licht has called Mayfield a franchise quarterback, but has not offered the veteran a long-term deal ahead of the 2026 season. Mayfield could be on his way out of Tampa in 2027 unless the team decides to use the franchise tag on him. Mayfield ranks 11th out of 40 qualifying QBs in adjusted EPA per drop back since the start of the 2024 season, ahead of Jalen Hurts and Dak Prescott, among others.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected TE Luke Musgrave (neck) to play at some point in 2026.
item.description:
Luke Musgrave GB Tight End

Musgrave is coming back from a neck injury with no clear timeline for a return to action. The Packers last week signed Jonnu Smith, who will play behind Tucker Kraft to start the regular season. Smith could be an interesting waiver add if Kraft — returning from a major knee injury — misses any time in 2026.

Source: Tom Silverstein

item.title: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

“Asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs, Gutekunst says he wants to let the process play out,” The Athletic’s Matt Schneidmann said. Jacobs on Sunday was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List while his legal situation plays out. Jacobs in May was arrested and booked on five charges, including felony strangulation. ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Monday that Jacobs’ time on the exempt list was, for now, indefinite, and hinged entirely on how his legal situation unfolds. If damning video evidence is released, Jacobs could miss most or all of the regular season. MarShawn Lloyd would start the year as Green Bay’s lead back and has a chance to be one of fantasy’s best running back values.

Source: Matt Schneidmann

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Cade Klubnik will be the team’s QB2 to start the regular season.
item.description:
Cade Klubnik NYJ Quarterback

What this means is that Geno Smith has plenty of job security. Klubnik in the preseason completed 21 of 34, passes for 190 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception while taking four sacks. Klubnik would be a marked downgrade from Smith if the veteran misses time in 2026.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Ravens signed K Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
item.description:
Jake Moody BAL Kicker

It’s an interesting move after Tyler Loop, the team’s Week 1 starter, struggled in training camp and during the preseason. The journeyman Moody was most recently cut by the Commanders and would only be activated to the 53-man roster if Loop’s struggles continue into the regular season. Last year with Washington, Moody went 10-for-11 while going 2-for-2 on distances of 50-plus yards.

Source: Jake Zrebiec

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Jeremiyah Love is “about 50/50" to play in Week 1 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love is still working his way back from a preseason high ankle sprain, and has been spotted doing some light practice work in recent days. The Cardinals will “have to see how he progresses” before they decided whether to make the rookie back active for Week 1. If Love is out for the season opener, Tyler Allgeier could see a heavy workload, as James Conner (ankle) begins the season on injured reserve.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Steelers general manager Omar Khan said the team would not engage in contract negotiations during the regular season.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

That could mean the team will have to hammer out a new deal with Joey Porter, Jr. before the season kicks off in less than two weeks. The Steelers recently activated Porter from the PUP list after he dealt with a supposed back injury in the offseason. Porter will most likely have to play out his rookie contract or hold out. He would be a big loss for the Pittsburgh defense.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Malik Nabers (knee) remains noncommittal about his Week 1 status.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers told reporters Monday that he still needed to clear a few checkpoints before being ready to suit up for the season opener against Dallas. “Will it take some time? Who knows?” he said. “But I know for sure if I’m out there, I’m going to run some routes.” Some routes and movements, he added, feel better than others on surgically-repaired knee. Even so, ESPN’s Jordan Raanan said the “expectation is [Nabers] will be playing barring some sort of setback.” A target hog who’s explosive with the ball in his hands, Nabers profiles as a risky fantasy selection for now. His absence in the season opener would be a blow to Jaxson Dart’s outlook.

The high ankle sprain suffered in the team’s first preseason game has the potential to cost Love regular season games considering the timing, but it sounds as if there is at least a sliver of hope that Love will not miss any regular season time. That said, there is also the possibility that Love is active come Week 1 but not at full strength, something that could realistically influence his workload early in the season. Fantasy managers will want to monitor the situation closely as the regular season approaches.

Source: Brooke Pryor

Jaydon Blue

It has been quite the fall from grace for Blue over the previous 24 hours, seemingly going from the favorite for backup duties for the Cowboys to without a home. It is also noteworthy that only one running back was claimed during the waiver period, veteran Emari Demercado, by this same Cowboys team. Blue appears to have lost all fantasy value and faces an uphill battle for a meaningful role in his sophomore campaign.

item.description:
Isaiah Bond CLE Wide Receiver

item.description:
Darrell Luter LV Cornerback

item.description:

Either way, Cook now gets a fresh start after four starts across five appearances for the Jets during his rookie season. Tight end Justin Joly also joins the Dolphins after being released by the Broncos. The team kept four tight ends through final cuts, making the path to a roster spot more muddied, but he lands on his feet after being forced to contemplate a potential practice squad spot in Denver. Zach Ertz

item.title: ESPN’s Brady Henderson believes the Seahawks will “roll with [Jadarian] Price as their lead back while mixing in a heavy dose of George Holani.”
item.description:
George Holani SEA Running Back

Holani, however, should see significant usage in the Seahawks backfield. His “receiving and pass-blocking skills seem perfectly suited for third-down work,” Henderson said. Emanuel Wilson, Henderson added, will be the “power complement to those two” if he’s fully recovered from an undisclosed injury. “Whatever plan Seattle has going into Week 1 will start to change once Charbonnet returns,” Henderson said. “Whenever Charbonnet is all the way back, it’s easy to envision the Seahawks splitting the work in their backfield fairly evenly between him and Price the way they did last season with Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III.” Sam Darnold has called Price a “special player” who excels as a pass catcher. item.description:
Michael Jurgens MIN Center

Jurgens will miss at least four games while on injured reserve. He appeared in 15 games last year and made three starts. Joe Huber will back up Blake Brandel to start the year.

item.title: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (calf) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

San Francisco also placed offensive lineman Austen Pleasants on injured reserve. Both players will miss at least four games to start the year. Kirk missed most of training camp with the calf issue. Mike Evans, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Deebo Samuel will start for the team in three-receiver sets. Even when Kirk comes back, he’s likely stuck as the WR4 on the depth chart.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Seahawks released CB Trevon Diggs.
item.description:
Trevon Diggs

Diggs, who doesn’t have an interception since the 2024 season, will likely latch on with another secondary in need of depth pieces. Diggs never had much of a chance of making the roster in Seattle, a defense sporting one of the league’s best coverage units. He totaled 31 pass breakups and 17 interceptions in his first three NFL seasons, from 2020-22. He’s totaled just six pass breakups and three interceptions since then. Diggs is entering his age-28 season.

Source: Greg Bell

Bryce Oliver

Quez Watkins

item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

The Bears also placed LB Noah Sewell (Achilles) and DL Shemar Turner (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. All three players must miss at least four games to begin the year.

Source: Chicago Bears

DeeJay Dallas

Dallas was the odd man out in the backfield after the signing of Chris Rodriguez, ultimately prompting his release. The team will move forward with Bhayshul Tuten, Rodriguez, and LeQuint Allen atop the depth chart entering the regular season. Salvon Ahmed CHI Running Back

Ahmed missed all of 2025 with an ankle injury. He joined the Bears in May, but did not make the team. item.description:
Travis Homer

Homer was fighting for an end-of-bench spot in the Steelers’ running back room. His release indicates they will keep Eli Heidenreich on the initial 53-man roster. Also waived/released by the Steelers were DL Kyler Baugh, DB Devan Boykin, DB Sebastian Castro, DL Anthony Goodlow, WR Max Hurleman, DB D’Shawn Jamison, OL Steven Jones, TE Lance Mason, TE Lake McRee, OL Doug Nester, RB Lew Nichols, DB Doneiko Slaughter, WR Brandon Smith, LB Julius Welschof, LB Jacoby Windmon, LB Malik Harrison, DL Esezi Otomewo, and LB Elandon Roberts.

item.title: Saints placed Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

Tyson has been dealing with hamstring issues since his senior season at Arizona State. The issue flared up during training camp and he is now expected to be sidelined for roughly two months, as of two weeks ago. With an international game in Week 7 and a bye the following week, a Week 9 return looks like the most likely outcome for the rookie. He could still put up strong fantasy numbers in the second half of the season, but it’s hard to justify holding him in leagues with shallow benches.

item.title: Steelers activated Joey Porter Jr. (back) from the active/PUP list.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter Jr. spent all of training camp on the PUP list with a back issue. He was also searching for a new contract without much luck, so it’s safe to assume the back and bank issues were related. Without much leverage in the situation, he is likely stuck playing out the 2026 season on his rookie deal.

item.title: Cardinals placed James Conner on injured reserve.
item.description:
James Conner ARI Running Back

Conner will miss at least four games to start the year as he continues to work his way back from the ankle injury that ended his 2025 season. The team can designate him to return after Week 4. With Jeremiyah Love also banged up, Tyler Allgeier could be in for a hefty workload early in the season.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Vikings waived RB Jermar Jefferson with an injury designation.
item.description:
Jermar Jefferson

Assuming Jefferson clears waivers, he will revert to the Vikings’ injured reserve list and likely be cut with an injury settlement. The Vikings also waived/released CB Da’Veawn Armstead, WR Michael Briscoe, G Henry Byrd, WR Terrill Davis, C Gavin Gerhardt, G Joshua Gray, S Kahlef Hailassie, CB Tre Hawkins, LB Bangally Kamara, TE Marshall Lang, TE Matt Lauter, G Vershon Lee, OL Tristan Leigh, OL Delby Lemieux, CB Bryce Phillips, OL Tomas Rimac, DL Jahvaree Ritzie, LB Josh Ross, WR Trayvon Rudolph, WR Marcus Sanders Jr., RB Zavier Scott, OLB Cam’Ron Stewart, DL Smith Vilbert, CB Jarod Washington, CB Marcus Allen, OLB Kenny Dyson Jr., WR Dontae Fleming, TE Bryson Nesbit, LB Jacob Roberts, DL Jonathan Harris, P Johnny Hekker, DL Isaiahh Loudermilk, and S Tavierre Thomas.

item.title: Dolphins claimed QB Brady Cook via waivers.
item.description:
Brady Cook MIA Quarterback

Cook joins starter Malik Willis and recent acquisition Kyle McCord in the pecking order at quarterback for the Dolphins, with the assumption that McCord will serve as the primary backup on game days during the regular season. Either way, Cook now gets a fresh start after four starts across five appearances for the Jets during his rookie season. Tight end Justin Joly also joins the Dolphins after being released by the Broncos. The team kept four tight ends through final cuts, making the path to a roster spot more muddied, but he lands on his feet after being forced to contemplate a potential practice squad spot in Denver. Also claimed were DB Marcellus Dial, T Chukwuebuka Godrick, T Jarrett Kingston, DB Reese Taylor, and DB Julius Wood.

item.title: Cowboys claimed RB Emari Demercado via waivers.
item.description:
Emari Demercado DAL Running Back

Demercado enters a wide open backfield depth chart behind starter Javonte Williams and primary backup Malik Davis, the two of whom were the only running backs to survive 53-man roster cuts Sunday. It does not appear the Cowboys are finished adding to their backfield, with most teams keeping four running backs on the active roster throughout the season. More to come.

item.title: Falcons released RB Tyler Goodson.
item.description:
Tyler Goodson

Goodson made an impact as part of the Falcons’ running back room in the preseason but ultimately Brian Robinson Jr. will keep the backup job. Also waived/released by the Falcons were CB Darnay Holmes, DT Eric Johnson II, TE Nick Muse, OLB Azeez Ojulari, DE Cam Sample, LB Channing Tindall, DT Marlon Tuipulotu, OL Brandon Walton, DL Chris Williams, LB Josh Woods, DT Carlos Allen, WR Vinny Anthony, OL James Brockermeyer, CB Cobee Bryant, RB Nate Carter, OL Kam Dewberry, WR Dylan Drummond, RB Cash Jones, OL Riley Mahlman, WR Keelan Marion, DT Devonnsha Maxwell, OT Wanya Morris, LB Daveren Rayner, OL Jaeden Roberts, TE Joshua Simon, DB Keidron Smith, OL Andrew Stueber, LB Bralen Trice, TE Jack Velling, WR Antwane Wells Jr., and CB A.J. Woods.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Dolphins waived RB Jarquez Hunter.
item.description:
Jarquez Hunter

It’s a bit surprising after Hunter was acquired in a 1-for-1 swap for Tutu Atwell three days ago, but the Dolphins are undoubtedly hoping he will clear waivers and revert to the practice squad. The move was also a Miami money-saver, so it was not all for naught. Also waived/released by the Dolphins are OT Gottlieb Ayedze, CB Miles Battle, S Major Burns, TE Jeremiah Franklin, QB Mark Gronowski, WR Donaven McCulley, EDGE Rodney McGraw, CB Jai’Onte’ McMillan, QB Cam Miller, DL Fatorma Mulbah, LB Cam Riley, RB Carlos Washington Jr., DL Matthew Butler, LB Tyrel Dodson, EDGE Cameron Goode, OT Charlie Heck, S Lonnie Johnson Jr., WR Terrace Marshall Jr., EDGE David Ojabo, WR Jalen Reagor and CB Marco Wilson.

item.title: Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Jeremy McNichols WAS Running Back

McNichols will start the season sidelined with a linger quad injury he suffered in mid-August. Used primarily as a pass-catching back, McNichols could see playing time later this season if Rachaad White or Jacory Croskey-Merritt miss any time. He will miss at least the first four games of the season and should remain on waivers.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Colts waived Blake Freeland.
item.description:
Blake Freeland

Indy drafted Freeland in the fourth round of the 2023 draft. He made nine starts as a rookie but only took the field for 23 offensive snaps in his second season. Freeland then missed the entirety of 2025 with a fracture in his right leg.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Giants released OL Evan Neal.
item.description:
Evan Neal

Neal was somewhat inexplicably given a one-year contract in early March after one of the more disastrous rookie contracts in recent memory, only to be released during final cuts. Perhaps the team thought the magnetic polarities of the Earth would swap between then and now. Even so, the veteran minimum contract extended to the former first-round pick doesn’t cut too deep. He’s only 25, so perhaps an offensive line-needy team will try their hand at a career resurgence, but we wouldn’t count on it.

item.title: 49ers released WR KhaDarel Hodge.
item.description:
KhaDarel Hodge

The Athletic’s Matt Barrows said Hodge is a “strong candidate” to land on the Niners’ practice squad headed into the regular season. A journyeman wideout who plays special teams, Hodge most recently played four seasons with the Falcons, never recording more than 14 receptions over that span. He could find his way onto the 49ers active roster if the team suffers more receiver injuries this year.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Lions S Kerby Joseph will begin the season on the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
Kerby Joseph DET Safety

Joseph is still nursing a knee injury that hampered him last season. He will remain on the PUP list to open the season, meaning he will miss a minimum of four games.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Steelers kept all four quarterbacks for the team’s initial 53-man roster.
item.description:
Will Howard PIT Quarterback

The Steelers will head into the regular season with Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and Drew Allar, who shined in training camp and during preseason outings in Mike McCarthy’s offense. If the 2026 season goes south for Pittsburgh, look for McCarthy to see what he has in Allar and perhaps Howard. Rudolph will likely back up Rodgers to start the regular season.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports J.J. McCarthy has made the Vikings’ initial 53-man roster.
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy MIN Quarterback

The Athletic’s Alec Lewis made a Saturday stir when he left McCarthy off his Vikings 53-man roster prediction, but that would have been hasty even if the Vikes are convinced “Nine” has no future with the organization. This keeps open the possibility of some sort of pick swap trade, or perhaps even “development” behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. We doubt coach Kevin O’Connell is holding his breath on that one. A manifest bust through his first two years in the league, McCarthy could also end up waived later this week after the Vikes make a few waiver claims. Even if his time in Minnesota has yet to come to an end, the clock is still ticking.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Panthers placed RB Travis Etienne on injured reserve.
item.description:
Trevor Etienne CAR Running Back

Etienne will be eligible to come off IR at some point during the 2026 regular season. He got some buzz during offseason workouts and training camp but has exceedingly little chance of seeing significant regular season snaps for Carolina. Etienne as a rookie in 2025 had 20 carries for 94 scoreless yards, functioning mostly as a kick returner.

Source: Panthers.com

item.title: Panthers acquired TeRah Edwards from the Chargers.
item.description:
TeRah Edwards CAR Defensive Lineman

The Chargers’ compensation for the move hasn’t been announced, but it’s certainly a Day Three pick swap. Edwards went undrafted last year and signed with the Chargers’ practice squad. He did not play in 2025. To be honest, we’re not really sure what the Panthers are doing here.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Giants released OL Evan Neal.
item.description:
Evan Neal

Seriously, obviously. Neal was somewhat inexplicably given a one-year contract in early March after one of the more disastrous rookie contracts in recent memory, only to be released during final cuts. Perhaps the team thought the magnetic polarities of the Earth would swap between then and now. Even so, the veteran minimum contract extended to the former first-round pick doesn’t cut too deep. Perhaps an offensive line-needy team will try their hand at a career resurgence, but we wouldn’t count on it.

item.title: Texans waived WR Lewis Bond.
item.description:
Lewis Bond

The No. 204 overall pick of the draft out of Boston College, Bond generated hype during the offseason program before turning in a solid preseason. It’s a bit of a surprise the receiver-needy Texans are passing on stashing him on the 53-man roster, but they will undoubtedly hope he clears waivers and lands on the practice squad.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Buccaneers released EDGE Chris Braswell.
item.description:
Chris Braswell

The 2024 second-round pick never fully caught on in Tampa and was buried on the depth chart, with the team’s selection of Reuben Bain in the first round effectively sealing his fate. Braswell is likely to draw interest in the open market and could catch on as a pass rush developmental depth piece in short order.

item.title: Saints placed Mason Tipton on the reserve/PUP list.
item.description:
